nodes.label: Sentinel Agent
nodes.author: Anirban Sarkar
nodes.rationale: Single-user, approval-gated investment intelligence agent: no existing tool aggregates Zerodha + INDmoney + Fidelity + EPF into one policy-bound view, and the owner wants every action human-approved and later scored.

nodes.label: ROE & ROCE Screen Fixture — Page 1
nodes.author: Mittal Analytics Private Limited
nodes.rationale: A real 42KB capture of screener.in's public 'ROE & ROCE' screen, page 1, 25 data rows. It exists because SCREENER_COLUMNS was written from imagination and parsed zero real rows — the parser is now driven by a real page rather than a hypothesis about one.

nodes.label: ROE & ROCE Screen Fixture — Page 2
nodes.author: Mittal Analytics Private Limited
nodes.rationale: The second page of the same capture, 25 rows, so pagination (?page=N, 25 rows/page, stop on a short page) is tested against real markup rather than a synthetic second page.

nodes.label: Sentinel Phase 2 Implementation Plan
nodes.rationale: Corrected against the PRD; explicitly refuses to introduce broker placement, execution bridge, real fills or a live advisory loop, and forbids resurrecting Kite OAuth as 'Phase 2 preparation'.

nodes.label: Sentinel Phase 2.5 ("Advise") Implementation Plan
nodes.rationale: Owner decision of 2026-09-17: the LLM makes BUY/SELL/HOLD/WAIT and timing decisions from validated candidates. It expressly refines PRD §6.7's narration-only reading without making deterministic sizing, scores, taxes, caps, staleness or approval optional.

nodes.label: no-catch-up architecture test
nodes.rationale: A real checker, not a stub: it walks src/**/*.ts off disk, builds the import graph and asserts the transitive reachers of funded-status.ts are exactly buckets.ts, notify/digest.ts and jobs/digest.ts. Adding a fourth reader must be a deliberate allowlist edit.

nodes.label: funded_status unreadable by sizing or risk
nodes.norm_label: funded_status unreadable by sizing or risk
nodes.rationale: Deliberately isolated so no catch-up behaviour can emerge: knowing it is behind must never make the agent size bigger. Enforced by an architecture test rather than convention.

nodes.label: Derive the actual side of an assertion from real data
nodes.norm_label: derive the actual side of an assertion from real data
nodes.rationale: A guard-rail test that hard-codes both sides tests nothing — this is how the plan's false claim that the seed breaches the Sammaan cap survived. Never hard-code a literal downstream of seed data; it goes stale silently. The deliberate exception is surplus.test.ts, whose literals fail loudly on purpose.

nodes.label: Never Widen a Test Band to Make Red Go Green
nodes.norm_label: never widen a test band to make red go green
nodes.rationale: A band may only move after proving the model is right and the band's premise wrong, and then it is surfaced to the owner rather than edited silently.

nodes.label: FX BLOCKs Every Weekend by Construction
nodes.norm_label: fx blocks every weekend by construction
nodes.rationale: FRESHNESS_HOURS.fx is 48h but frankfurter publishes ECB rates on weekdays only, so a normal Fri-to-Mon gap is ~72h: the fetch is fine and the limit is wrong for the publication calendar. Same 'widen the band vs fix the model' call as the digest cron test — do not just raise 48h without deciding which it is.

nodes.label: Screener Screen Table Markup Contract
nodes.rationale: Rows are identified by data-row-company-id and columns by a th data-tooltip attribute (Current Price, Price to Earning, Market Capitalization, Dividend yield, Net Profit latest quarter, YOY Quarterly profit growth, Sales latest quarter, YOY Quarterly sales growth, Return on capital employed, Return on equity, Average return on equity 3Years/5Years). Some owner screens render tooltip-less headers, which is why normalizeHeader needs a visible-text alias path; the company link slug is the only identity screener exports, since it publishes no ticker.

nodes.label: Phase 1 Complete (Tasks 1-13)
nodes.rationale: Task 13 found two pieces recorded as shipped in Task 3 that did not exist — downloadBhavcopy always threw and downloadIndexSeries was never written — so the daily sync recorded a successful nse-bhavcopy step having done nothing: the silent degradation PRD 8.2 exists to forbid, inside the job whose whole contract is loud failure.

nodes.label: Screener Screen HTML Scraper (post-Phase-1)
nodes.rationale: screener.in's CSV export is paywalled but a public screen URL is not, so parseScreenHtml reads the rendered table directly; re-importing the same (as_of, filename) deletes the prior batch because screener_uploads is append-only and ON CONFLICT cannot update.

nodes.label: Four Artifacts Written From Imagination and Presented as Spec
nodes.norm_label: four artifacts written from imagination and presented as spec
nodes.rationale: The 40 watchlist names, SCREENER_COLUMNS, the 'shipped' screener staleness check and the 'shipped' bhavcopy downloader were all invented and recorded as delivered. Anything describing an EXTERNAL format or universe is a hypothesis until it has touched the real thing, and a ledger entry is a lead, never evidence — grep for the symbol.

nodes.label: ISIN Backfill Is Fill-Only, Never Clobber
nodes.norm_label: isin backfill is fill-only, never clobber
nodes.rationale: Only NSE:% ids with NULL/empty isin are filled from EQUITY_L.csv, never overwriting an owner-verified seeded value, and backfilling cannot create an instrument. Caveat: re-seeding overwrites backfilled values because seed.ts upserts isin = excluded.isin.

nodes.label: LLM Shortlists the Watchlist, Engine Owns Every Number
nodes.norm_label: llm shortlists the watchlist, engine owns every number
nodes.rationale: The division that keeps PRD 6.7 intact: the model proposes names and one sentence of reasoning while the engine decides everything carrying a number. Enforced in code, not trusted to the prompt — a pick must already exist in instruments, held names are excluded, and rows land as proposals awaiting sign-off.

nodes.label: NSE Bhavcopy Archive-First With Whole-Market Fallback
nodes.norm_label: nse bhavcopy archive-first with whole-market fallback
nodes.rationale: The archive host 404s every 2026 date while still serving 2019-2024, so equity prices had silently stopped landing in June. Archive stays primary because it is the only shape carrying an ISIN column; the fallback uses a NUMERIC month (the alphabetic-month name 404s there) and full-market rows are resolved through the NSE:<symbol> id instruments already carry. Both missing returns empty and is still reported honestly.

nodes.label: NSE Trading Calendar and isTradingDay
nodes.rationale: The weekend-only rule was wrong in both directions: it asked NSE for a file on ~15 holidays and would have skipped Sunday Muhurat trading when the exchange IS open. The asymmetry sets the bar for adding a date — a missing holiday costs one loud failed step, a wrong holiday silently starves every price-dependent engine, so when in doubt leave it out.

nodes.label: One Model Family, Split by Capability (text vs vision)
nodes.norm_label: one model family, split by capability (text vs vision)
nodes.rationale: The finance model is text-only and physically 400s on an image upload, so TEXT_MODEL is kept out of VISION_MODEL_CHAIN by test; vision reverted to the proven gemma leader after the vl trial. Tests assert wiring by DERIVING from the constants, never by restating a model id — the two that hard-coded a model id went red on the swap.

nodes.label: Screener Cohort Promotion (screen rows become instruments)
nodes.norm_label: screener cohort promotion (screen rows become instruments)
nodes.rationale: Identity is an inference, not a fact: NSE:<slug> is trusted only to be internally consistent with bhavcopy resolution, the name comes from the screen, and ISIN is deliberately left NULL for backfill:isin rather than invented. Degenerate /company/id/<n>/ rows resolving to slug 'ID' are refused because the LIKE fallback once substring-matched NSE:LIQUIDBEES.

nodes.label: SCREENER_COLUMNS Spec Was Written From Imagination
nodes.norm_label: screener_columns spec was written from imagination
nodes.rationale: A real screen overlaps SCREENER_COLUMNS on P/E alone, so a real export parses to zero usable rows; Symbol, Industry, FCF 5Y and Red Flags have no native column while the quality gate reads two of them. Deliberately not patched by guessing a second mapping — it needs one real exported file plus an owner decision.

nodes.label: parseScreenPaste (signed-in CSV/TSV path)
nodes.rationale: The public page serves only 13 old columns; Profit Var 5Yrs %, Sales Var 5Yrs % and Free Cash Flow 5Yrs exist only in the signed-in author view, so the owner's export is the live test. Delimiter is auto-detected and repeated header rows reset the column map because screener repeats headers every ~15 rows on paginated exports.

nodes.label: The Starter Watchlist Has an LLM-Origination Problem
nodes.norm_label: the starter watchlist has an llm-origination problem
nodes.rationale: All 40 seeded rows are labelled source 'advisor' but were written by an LLM from training recall with no market data; the engine scores only what sits in that table, so the LLM originated the universe even though it never originates a score — in tension with PRD 6.7.

nodes.label: Workflow Schedules and Digest-on-Sync Gating
nodes.rationale: digest.yml lost its fixed cron and fires on workflow_run of sync gated on success, with the trade-off accepted that a failed sync means no digest that day; sync moved to 19:00 IST so it runs after NSE publishes the whole-market file around 18:00.

nodes.label: Screener Gate Inputs — Owner Decision
nodes.rationale: Screener has no native column for FCF 5Y or Red Flags. FCF was settled by the owner adding Free Cash Flow 5Yrs to the screen; Red Flags settled as per-company manual review with the gate treating NULL as a NOTE rather than a failure.

nodes.label: Cash Ceiling Owner Amendment (out of band)
nodes.norm_label: cash ceiling owner amendment (out of band)
nodes.rationale: Written TDD with four tests red first; a pre-existing test named 'honours a changed rail' asserted only toBeDefined() and passed against code that read nothing, so it was rewritten to prove a DB value actually changes the verdict. The B3 collision was surfaced to the owner, not silently absorbed.

nodes.label: Phase 2 Task 1 — Paper Approval State Machine
nodes.norm_label: phase 2 task 1 — paper approval state machine
nodes.rationale: FR-20-25 advisory path ACKNOWLEDGED to AWAITING_MANUAL_EXECUTION to VERIFIED/ABANDONED, defer resurfacing with composite-score check, and paper simulations; limit-order expiry deferred because the PRD is silent.

nodes.label: Phase 2 Task 2 — Rails, Freeze, Breaker
nodes.rationale: checkRails, checkPortfolioRails, freeze/unfreeze with typed confirmation, a three-falsification breaker with mandatory post-mortem, 48h cooling on rail changes and drawdown gating at 15%/20%.

nodes.label: Phase 2 Task 4 — Web Approval/Cleanup/Rail Surfaces
nodes.rationale: Every API action writes an append-only order_transitions row plus an audit_log entry and mirrors the Telegram bot's platform functions, so the two surfaces cannot drift.

nodes.label: funded_status Firewall (no catch-up behaviour)
nodes.rationale: A sizing or risk function that learns how funded the owner is would start taking more risk to catch up; the constraint is enforced by an import-graph architecture test (Task 10) rather than by the type system, because a branded number is still assignable to a plain number parameter.

nodes.label: TDD With Mutation-Checked Guard Rails
nodes.rationale: A guard-rail test that hard-codes both sides of its comparison tests nothing; one side must be derived from the real data structure and the test mutation-checked to prove it can go red.

nodes.label: B3 Emergency Fund Excluded From the Cash Ceiling
nodes.norm_label: b3 emergency fund excluded from the cash ceiling
nodes.rationale: Holding the emergency fund the IPS mandates is compliance, not idleness, and the 6L target is 10.7% of the 55.97L base so a funded B3 would trip the rail. Only the funded balance in bucket_flows is excused, never the target; bucket_flows is queried directly because buckets.ts re-exports the reporting-only FI metric and the firewall test refuses a risk function any path to it — including the identifier appearing in a comment.

nodes.label: Cash Ceiling Owner Rail (10%)
nodes.rationale: The PRD gave no cash number and the seeded 20% was invented; the owner set 10% on 2026-09-19 as an amendment, written byte-identically into PRD 3.3 and src/config/ips-v1.ts so ips-verbatim fails if they drift. CASH is classify()'s CASH class only, so EPF, bonds and liquid/debt funds do not count.

nodes.label: FI Corpus Band (income varies, SWR is a separate axis)
nodes.norm_label: fi corpus band (income varies, swr is a separate axis)
nodes.rationale: The shipped code took one income and varied only the SWR, so stretch came back BELOW the floor target and stretchRatio exceeded floorRatio for every input — the owner would have read 'better funded against the harder goal'. buckets.ts now re-exports the single model so the funded-status allowlist cannot be sidestepped through buckets.fundedRatio.

nodes.label: The Rails Engine Reports, It Does Not Gate
nodes.norm_label: the rails engine reports, it does not gate
nodes.rationale: checkRails is imported by digest.ts and never called; validateOrderGate checks staleness and FR-11/12 structure only; checkFreeze/setFreeze/recordFalsification are referenced only by their own tests; last_rail_change has three readers and no writer. The only live path is checkPortfolioRails feeding the digest breach list and /rails, so the Phase 2 ledger's 'rails enforced' must not be read as enforced on the order path.

nodes.label: settings_rails Keys Carry Their Unit in the Name
nodes.norm_label: settings_rails keys carry their unit in the name
nodes.rationale: _pct is a percent and _paise is money; the retired dotted cash.ceiling was a bare fraction. The /rails page pushed everything through a x100 Pct formatter and printed the new percent-valued rail as 1000.0%, so it now formats by key suffix.

nodes.label: checkPortfolioRails False TACTICAL_BUDGET_EXCEEDED
nodes.rationale: It sums the whole EQUITY/ETF/MF book's market value against a per-month flow budget — a stock compared to a flow — so it fires permanently for any portfolio over 50k. The per-order version in checkRails is correct. Not yet fixed.

nodes.label: FR-34 Cooling-Off Unimplemented; Rails Gate Nothing
nodes.norm_label: fr-34 cooling-off unimplemented; rails gate nothing
nodes.rationale: Investigated while deciding whether to backfill a cooling row. This bears directly on the Phase 2 DoD line 'a simulated rail violation and breaker trip both behave to spec': they behave to spec in tests that call the functions directly, and nothing in the running system calls them. Arguably the Phase 3 blocker, since Phase 3 is the first phase where an unblocked order reaches a broker.

nodes.label: Seven Owner Rails Are Still Constants in Code
nodes.norm_label: seven owner rails are still constants in code
nodes.rationale: PRD 11 says all rails live in settings_rails but only cash_ceiling_pct does; four seeded values contradict the PRD, so wiring the rest to the table means fixing those four first — copying the constants across would loosen the employer cap.

nodes.label: Task 2: Rails, Freeze, Breaker, Behavioral Protocol
nodes.norm_label: task 2: rails, freeze, breaker, behavioral protocol
nodes.rationale: Breaker counts distinct approved recommendations' falsification outcomes, not duplicate events or individual legs, so replayed or duplicate observations cannot fabricate a streak.

nodes.label: Deterministic Actionable Sizing
nodes.rationale: Missing capability: allocation drift paise is not a general satellite/exit unit sizer, and a signal score is not a budget. The combined selected batch plus outstanding reservations must be validated so two individually safe candidates cannot spend the same money.

nodes.label: Phase 2.5 Owner Inputs Gate
nodes.rationale: Satellite per-action sizing budget, news source scope and freshness SLA, manual rating/G-sec review cadence, and shortlist regeneration must come from the owner; the plan withholds the affected capability rather than inventing a default.
nodes.source_location: Owner inputs before the affected capability is enabled

nodes.label: Allocation / Drift Engine
nodes.rationale: Hybrid rebalancing: annual April calendar rebalance plus monthly ±5% drift bands; a band breach generates a recommendation, never an auto-trade, and prefers directing new flows over selling for tax reasons.

nodes.label: Bucket B3: Emergency Fund
nodes.rationale: ₹6L liquid, funded by the Sammaan Sep-2026 maturity plus the Nov-2026 vest; it is the structural fix for the 2022 liquidity crisis that caused the SIP pause. Split across banks beyond ₹5L for DICGC cover.

nodes.label: Behavioral Pre-Commitment Protocol
nodes.rationale: At −20% drawdown the agent replays the owner's own written policy and 2022 history and demands a typed reason before any pause — designed around the finding that the 2022 SIP pause was a liquidity crisis, not fear.

nodes.label: Cash Ceiling (≤10% idle cash)
nodes.rationale: Measured on bank balances less the funded B3 balance only — the B3 target is never excused — because idle cash above the ceiling is uninvested capital, while an unfunded emergency target is not yet cash set aside.

nodes.label: 30% Maximum Drawdown Constraint
nodes.rationale: Revealed rather than questionnaire-derived tolerance; it is the binding constraint that sets the ~60% equity ceiling.

nodes.label: /freeze Kill Switch
nodes.rationale: One Telegram command cancels all pending approvals and halts drafting; notifications continue during freeze so the owner is never blinded by the safety action itself.

nodes.label: Never-Events (F&O, intraday, leverage, LAS)
nodes.rationale: Implemented as absent code paths rather than disabled features, with no override path in software, so a future moment of weakness cannot toggle them on.

nodes.label: Safety Rails Engine
nodes.rationale: Rails live in settings_rails and are enforced pre-draft in deterministic code, never LLM-evaluated; a draft violating a rail cannot exist. Edits cool for 48h and loosening is refused outright above 15% drawdown.

nodes.label: Strategic Asset Allocation
nodes.rationale: Equity ceiling ~60% calibrated so a 2008-grade crash lands at roughly −25 to −30% portfolio drawdown, matching the stated tolerance; gold 5–10%; EPF counts as debt-like.

nodes.label: Objective Function (risk-adjusted return under 30% drawdown)
nodes.rationale: Maximize risk-adjusted return subject to a hard 30% max drawdown; the 30% number comes from the owner's revealed tolerance rather than a questionnaire.

nodes.label: No Trading Paths (absent code, not disabled features)
nodes.norm_label: no trading paths (absent code, not disabled features)
nodes.rationale: F&O, intraday, leverage and LAS are absent code paths rather than flagged-off features, so there is no override flag that a bug or a prompt could flip.

nodes.label: Fidelity RSU Ingestion Flow
nodes.rationale: Proposals are priced with the SAME UNITS_SCALE/toUnitsMicros that rsu.ts exports, so the proposal's gross equals confirmVest's recomputed gross and net <= gross passes by construction. Grants are never auto-created (FR-02) and skipped entries are consumed so a stuck entry cannot silently block later confirmations.

nodes.label: Bond invested_amount Is Face Value, Not Cost
nodes.norm_label: bond invested_amount is face value, not cost
nodes.rationale: The API returns units x face, so the shipped mapper wrote face value straight into cost; aggregate() now returns avgCostPaise = null for every BOND row. total_pnl is computed against face too and understates true unrealised by 20,000.43, and the payload returns a stale pre-rebrand issuer name, so the single-issuer cap cannot be derived from it.

nodes.label: INDmoney MCP networth_holdings Contract
nodes.rationale: The original mapper was written against an invented fixture and its three tests passed by feeding the invention back to itself. Real contract: asset_type is required, the reply is an envelope, invested_amount can be the string 'unknown', investment_code is polymorphic, the same instrument arrives once per broker/folio and MUST be aggregated, and a rate-limited call returns successfully with an error object — reading that as 'no holdings' would wipe the portfolio, so it is fatal.

nodes.label: Kite Retired — INDmoney Is the Only Portfolio Source
nodes.norm_label: kite retired — indmoney is the only portfolio source
nodes.rationale: Kite worked on its first real run and that is how the bug surfaced: INDmoney already aggregates the same Zerodha account, so net worth jumped 26% with no money moving. Owner chose to drop Kite rather than build a precedence rule; the token also expired daily with no refresh token, making unattended sync impossible anyway.

nodes.label: loadPositions Reconciles Seed vs Live Only
nodes.norm_label: loadpositions reconciles seed vs live only
nodes.rationale: Live-live rows are never merged — each source manages its own aggregation — which is correct while INDmoney is the sole live source but silently sums the moment a second live source covers the same account. The precondition now lives in the docstring so the next source cannot repeat it.

nodes.label: Owner True-Up Items
nodes.rationale: Open data questions that need real statements and must never be guessed: the RSU per-grant split (57.05L modelled vs PRD 53.25L), the missing milestones.raised_on column (the old hard-coded date was a fabricated figure shown to the owner as fact), the unsourced DEBT floor and CASH ceiling bands, basket decomposition, and the whole Indian equity book having no cost basis.

nodes.label: RSU Vest Projection (cumulative tranche allocation)
nodes.rationale: Tranches are allocated cumulatively so 16 parts always sum back to the whole grant; rounding each independently (the plan's sketch) leaves a projection whose parts need not add to its whole. FR-03 is enforced in SQL by a unique (grant_id, vest_on) + conditional upsert, because the original read-then-write was check-then-act and a confirmVest landing in the window left an ACTUAL-labelled row carrying model numbers.

nodes.label: Seed/Live Double-Count and the Reconciliation
nodes.rationale: Two live causes: id namespaces do not meet (only 3 of 47 rows carry an ISIN) and nothing ever retires manual-seed. Owner decision: the live source wins per (canonicalInstrumentId, account), but a holding a live source stops reporting falls back to the seed row rather than vanishing, which is safer against a partial API reply since staleness already flags the source.

nodes.label: Real Fidelity Statement Is the Live Test
nodes.norm_label: real fidelity statement is the live test
nodes.rationale: The next statement screenshot both exercises the shipped RSU flow end to end and resolves the per-grant split true-up, because it carries per-grant units and vest dates — the exact data the gap asks for. Never tune the model toward the PRD value.

nodes.label: Db Four-Method Interface
nodes.rationale: query/exec/withTransaction/close is the shipped interface, not the obsolete two-method plan sketch; withTransaction pins one connection and does not nest, and ::jsonb params take objects because postgres-js otherwise stores opaque JSON strings.

nodes.label: Paper Execution Simulator
nodes.rationale: Simulates session-missing, partial fill, verbatim broker rejection and market closure without any broker dependency or real holdings/lots/cash writes.

nodes.label: Task 1: Paper Orders + Approval State Machine
nodes.norm_label: task 1: paper orders + approval state machine
nodes.rationale: Execution-side states are paper simulator events only; the simulator cannot be selected as a live execution adapter.

nodes.label: advisor_proposals (immutable)
nodes.rationale: Signed/dismissed status is derived from append-only decision events; there is no UPDATE of a supposedly append-only payload/status row. Unavailable token usage is NULL, never an invented zero.

nodes.label: Approval State Machine
nodes.rationale: DRAFT → PENDING_APPROVAL → APPROVED/MODIFIED/DEFERRED/REJECTED/EXPIRED, then AWAITING_SESSION → EXECUTING → fills, with a separate advisory path ending in VERIFIED or ABANDONED.

nodes.label: Audit Immutability
nodes.rationale: Append-only tables with RLS denying update/delete; nothing is ever hard-deleted, so every state transition remains reconstructible after the fact.

nodes.label: Order Idempotency Tags
nodes.rationale: Every order carries a UUID tag checked before placement and reused on retry, so replaying the same approval can never produce two broker orders.

nodes.label: Paper Mode
nodes.rationale: A global flag under which the full pipeline runs, recommendations are scored, and execution is structurally impossible; 4 weeks minimum before any live drafting.

nodes.label: Staleness Engine
nodes.rationale: Every datum carries as_of + source; prices 24h, NAVs 48h, fundamentals 1 quarter, FX 48h, syncs 36h. Violations block recommendations loudly — free-data fragility is mitigated by guaranteeing loud failure rather than silent degradation.

nodes.label: Supabase Storage Schema
nodes.rationale: Minimum table set spanning snapshots, lots, recommendations, approvals, orders, scores, incidents, settings_rails and audit_log; free-tier pause risk mitigated by daily cron writes plus a weekly keep-alive ping.

nodes.label: Immutable History vs Current State
nodes.rationale: Immutable order intent/revision records plus append-only transition events, with current status derived through a reader/view — because putting an append-only trigger on a row and then UPDATE-ing its status is a contradiction. Modifications append a revision and invalidate the prior approval.

nodes.label: sync workflow
nodes.rationale: Runs `pnpm sync` daily at 13:30 UTC with DATABASE_URL and TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY; the only path that refreshes holdings, FX, EOD prices and NAVs.

nodes.label: digest workflow (daily digest delivery)
nodes.rationale: No fixed cron — triggered by workflow_run on sync success, so the digest never reads a stale snapshot. A failed sync means no digest that day, which is the intended loud failure.

nodes.label: FR-31 staleness gate
nodes.rationale: Every source carries a freshness limit. You cannot act on what cannot be valued today, so a lapsed source withdraws the names that depend on it rather than letting them be scored on old data.

nodes.label: pnpm digest
nodes.rationale: Composes and sends the daily digest via Telegram; DRY_RUN=1 prints to stdout and never calls Telegram, so placeholder credentials suffice locally.

nodes.label: pnpm sync
nodes.rationale: Syncs holdings from INDmoney, FX, NSE bhavcopy plus index, and AMFI NAVs.

nodes.label: index.md repo map
nodes.rationale: Read at session start in place of the ~4,700-line plan; lists every module's exports and role so the agent never has to re-read the plan end to end.

nodes.label: Workflow schedule table
nodes.rationale: The single place the cron times, triggers and reasons for ci / sync / digest / weekly / keepalive / screener-reminder are recorded together.

nodes.label: Daily-not-weekday sync cron, after NSE publication
nodes.norm_label: daily-not-weekday sync cron, after nse publication
nodes.rationale: A weekday-only sync left the Monday 03:15 digest reading Friday's data — 63.25h against a 36h freshness limit — so one digest in five was a guaranteed false staleness alarm. The band was right; the schedule was wrong. 19:00 IST = 13:30 UTC because NSE's whole-market file only lands after ~18:00 IST; an earlier run 404s it and prices_eod stays empty.

nodes.label: packageManager as the single pnpm version source
nodes.norm_label: packagemanager as the single pnpm version source
nodes.rationale: No workflow pins `version:` on pnpm/action-setup — package.json's `packageManager` is authoritative. Specifying both makes the action fail with 'Multiple versions of pnpm specified', which would break every workflow at setup.

nodes.label: Phase 1 provisioning items unverified against live sources
nodes.norm_label: phase 1 provisioning items unverified against live sources
nodes.rationale: NSE bhavcopy and index URLs are unverified against live NSE, AMFI is fixture-verified only, the holidays table is empty so only weekends are skipped, and GSEC_YIELD_PCT awaits owner input. Each fails loudly, but loudly still means a week of no data.

nodes.label: Sentinel SDD Progress Ledger
nodes.rationale: One line per task / defect / decision; details live in MEMORY.md, not here.

nodes.label: PENDING — Open Items and Watch List
nodes.norm_label: pending — open items and watch list

nodes.label: Money Is Never a Float
nodes.rationale: Branded bigint paise/cents only; float arithmetic on money silently loses or invents rupees and cannot be audited.

nodes.label: Session End Protocol
nodes.rationale: State files are updated in the SAME commit as the work so the ledger cannot drift from the code; MEMORY only takes durable facts, index only structural changes.

nodes.label: Session Start Protocol
nodes.rationale: Four short state files (PENDING, MEMORY, index, progress) are read in full every session so context is rebuilt cheaply; the 4,700-line plan is deliberately NOT re-read end to end because length is a tax on every session.

nodes.label: Single-User, No Multi-Tenancy
nodes.rationale: No accounts, no sharing; features that make recommendations easier to share are refused because they would turn a personal agent into unlicensed advice.

nodes.label: Money Primitives (Paise/Cents branded bigint)
nodes.rationale: mulP goes through integer micros truncating toward zero and parseMinorUnits rejects sub-paise precision, so no rounding ever happens in floating point.

nodes.label: Phase 2 Task 3 — Legacy Cleanup + Multi-Year LTCG Calendar
nodes.norm_label: phase 2 task 3 — legacy cleanup + multi-year ltcg calendar
nodes.rationale: All output is FR-11 paper recommendations with two alternates; unknown cost basis surfaces as an owner prerequisite rather than zero, and no run executes cleanup, disposes lots or consumes a real exemption.

nodes.label: Phase 2 Task 5 — Scheduling, Scoring and Backup/Restore Proof
nodes.norm_label: phase 2 task 5 — scheduling, scoring and backup/restore proof
nodes.rationale: Every scheduled action is idempotent via an idempotency key or an existing-simulation check; the restore script is the proof that the encrypted weekly dump is recoverable, verifying table counts, immutability triggers and RLS.

nodes.label: No Autonomous Execution
nodes.rationale: Every order requires fresh human approval; standing auto-execute rules are forbidden because the approval gate IS the safety model.

nodes.label: Allocation Engine (one net-worth basis, tax preference)
nodes.norm_label: allocation engine (one net-worth basis, tax preference)
nodes.rationale: Two independent numbers describing one portfolio is how a caller gets silently wrong percentages, so rebalanceRec throws when positions disagree with netWorth. Tax awareness is one preference, not an engine: dilute with new money before selling, order trims losses-first with unknown cost basis last, and TAX_POLICY_NOTE states plainly what is NOT computed because we hold aggregated positions, not per-lot acquisition dates.

nodes.label: FR-11/FR-12 Recommendation Objects + Paper Mode
nodes.rationale: A1 falls back to the index route because buying the market is the honest expression of 'we want this exposure but have no edge on which name carries it'; A2 must carry a different intent and defaults to do-nothing priced as a real option. Every IPS citation is validated against the rendered clause index — a citation the owner cannot look up is worse than none. FR-12 caps LOG to suppressed_actions rather than dropping, and paper mode defaults TRUE when the rail is absent.

nodes.label: Sell / Exit Triggers (section 6.5) and the Falsification Grammar
nodes.norm_label: sell / exit triggers (section 6.5) and the falsification grammar
nodes.rationale: recommendations.primary_rec carries a closed falsification grammar; a condition naming a datum we do not hold is untestable and returns null, because false and unknown are different answers. Only triggers 1-3 override the IPS 3.7 twelve-month hold; 4 and 5 surface with blockedByMinimumHold so the owner sees the engine wanted out and the IPS said wait. Data is cut at month END.

nodes.label: Signal Engine (section 6 quality gate + composite)
nodes.rationale: Two different 'no score' shapes on purpose: blocked by a stale input returns null (no score exists), a failed quality gate returns a row with qualityPassed false so the weekly report can say WHY a name was rejected. The gate fails closed on unknowns, mirroring FR-02. What it cannot see (EV/EBITDA, a name's own 5y P/E range, the G-sec yield) is declared rather than faked.

nodes.label: Credit-Rating Actions Have No Source (IPS 3.8)
nodes.rationale: Sell trigger 7 covers maturities only; the standing 3.8 review items cannot be watched automatically, so the owner must choose a manual quarterly review or a rating source in a later phase.

nodes.label: 10Y G-Sec Yield Has No Ingestion Source
nodes.norm_label: 10y g-sec yield has no ingestion source
nodes.rationale: The valuation leg scores earnings yield against it, so it is a required caller input; the number is the owner's, not one the engine may invent, and it is not a PRD 15.2 planning constant so it does not belong in ASSUMPTIONS.

nodes.label: Phase 2 Task 6 — Provisioning, Handoff and Phase 2 Acceptance
nodes.norm_label: phase 2 task 6 — provisioning, handoff and phase 2 acceptance
nodes.rationale: Tests cannot replace four elapsed weeks of paper operation or five real owner approval interactions, so the Phase 2 DoD stays open and the owner's paper-scorecard review gates Phase 3.

nodes.label: Web App Build Fix (out of band)
nodes.norm_label: web app build fix (out of band)
nodes.rationale: Rejected from the prior draft: a mock Db returning empty rows at build time and MOCK_APPROVED/MOCK_REJECTED responses — an approval endpoint that answers success when it cannot reach the database is the one thing this product must never do.

nodes.label: Audit Immutability (append-only + RLS)
nodes.rationale: Triggers must cover UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE (Postgres does not fire DELETE triggers on TRUNCATE) plus RLS, so the audit trail cannot be rewritten by any path.

nodes.label: .env Values Must Be Unquoted
nodes.rationale: Node's --env-file strips quotes but a hand-rolled loader (web/next.config.ts) does not, so a quoted api_key produced api_key=%22...%22 and a live Kite InputException. A UTF-8 BOM in front of the first KEY= would make that key silently invisible.

nodes.label: Scoring Harness (section 13 calibration)
nodes.rationale: The creation snapshot is immutable in SQL — UPDATE is allowed only on the eval columns — because blanket append-only made evals unwritable while dropping the trigger would let a bad week be re-based after the fact. An unscoreable call is recorded with its reason and never counted as a miss; below MIN_EVALS_FOR_CALIBRATION the table says 'insufficient data' rather than a percentage.

nodes.label: TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY Rotation
nodes.rationale: The old key was found in plaintext in this repo's own Claude Code transcripts; recovery was possible and deliberately declined in favour of rotation. A recover-key.yml workflow that echoed the secret into a run log was written and deleted unrun — it converts one lost secret into a permanent leak.

nodes.label: Next.js web/ Bundling Contract
nodes.rationale: web/ was never typechecked and imported three symbols that did not exist. Nothing in src/ may read a file at module scope because webpack rewrites new URL(..., import.meta.url) into an inert asset handle and Vercel never ships the file; every page carries force-dynamic so next build opens no DB connection.

nodes.label: Weekly Deep Report + Narration (FR-51)
nodes.rationale: FR-31 covers yesterday's recommendations too: an open recommendation whose instrument is blocked today is withheld, not deleted, because you cannot act on what you cannot value. Narration receives finished engine output and nothing feeds back, so a missing narrative never costs the owner the report. Blank GSEC_YIELD_PCT means NOT CONFIGURED, never 0, because a 0% risk-free rate scores every name as cheap.

nodes.label: Calibration Minimum N = 20 (owner true-up)
nodes.rationale: A stake in the ground, not a derived figure: at 4 recommendations/month it is about half a year of output per conviction bucket, and below it one outcome moves the hit-rate by more than 5 points.

nodes.label: Vercel Deploy — Owner Step Outstanding
nodes.rationale: The dependency half is fixed (postgres and pglite are now direct web/ deps rather than resolving by walking up to the repo-root node_modules), but the project still needs Root Directory = web WITH 'include source files outside the Root Directory' enabled, because the app imports ../../src/**.

nodes.label: Known defect: TACTICAL_BUDGET_EXCEEDED fires permanently
nodes.rationale: checkPortfolioRails compares the whole equity book's market value against the Rs 50k/month tactical flow budget — a stock-versus-flow comparison — so the rail is always in violation.

nodes.label: blockedInstruments (valuation-input blocking)
nodes.rationale: Blocks on valuation inputs, not just the portfolio source: the position's own portfolio feed, FX for anything non-INR, NAV for funds, prices for equity/ETF/bond, fundamentals for equity. A blocked name is not scored at all, and an open recommendation raised before the lapse is withheld and listed under staleness.

nodes.label: Composite score (valuation 30 / trend 30 / earnings 20 / fit 20)
nodes.rationale: Banded HIGH / MEDIUM / WATCH / NONE; only MEDIUM-or-better becomes an FR-11 recommendation.

nodes.label: FR-11 recommendation object (primary + exactly two alternates)
nodes.norm_label: fr-11 recommendation object (primary + exactly two alternates)
nodes.rationale: A1 is the same intent through a different instrument or the broad-index route; A2 is a different intent defaulting to doing nothing. Each carries a thesis under 150 words and at least one IPS clause that must actually exist in src/config/ips-v1.md — forcing the alternates keeps a single recommendation from reading as the only option.

nodes.label: FR-12 action caps
nodes.rationale: Four per calendar month and no repeat BUY on a name inside twelve months, overridable only by an IPS spec change, a material adverse falsification, or an owner directive.

nodes.label: IPS v1 verbatim text
nodes.rationale: PRD sections 3.1-3.10 stored verbatim and rendered via renderIps. A paraphrase at minus-20% drawdown is a product failure — the exact wording is the binding contract when it matters most.

nodes.label: IPS 3.7 twelve-month minimum hold and its overrides
nodes.norm_label: ips 3.7 twelve-month minimum hold and its overrides
nodes.rationale: Only thesis falsification, a red-flag event or a hard-cap breach override the hold. Other exit triggers (sustained underperformance, a better alternative) are still surfaced flagged blockedByMinimumHold, so the owner sees the engine wanted out and the policy said wait.

nodes.label: Section 6 quality gate (fail-closed)
nodes.rationale: ROCE, five-year FCF, D/E with a finance-sector waiver and screener red flags, all fail-closed on an unknown — an absent metric is a fail, never an assumed pass.

nodes.label: suppressed_actions (capped actions are logged, never dropped)
nodes.norm_label: suppressed_actions (capped actions are logged, never dropped)
nodes.rationale: A capped action is written to suppressed_actions and shown in the report so the owner can see the engine wanted to act and the cap said no.

nodes.label: Rails hard-coded despite PRD 11 saying they live in settings_rails
nodes.norm_label: rails hard-coded despite prd 11 saying they live in settings_rails
nodes.rationale: Only cash_ceiling_pct is actually read from settings_rails; every other rail is a hard-coded literal or a CAPS constant, and RAIL_CONSTRAINTS is exported and imported by nobody.

nodes.label: Bucket B2: House Fund
nodes.rationale: Hyderabad home 2033–35; 100% capital-preservation once seeded — no equity risk on money needed within 7 years of purchase.

nodes.label: Hard Concentration Caps
nodes.rationale: ≤10% single stock/issuer, ≤35% single MF scheme, ≤25% sector, ≤10% employer stock (NOW) — the NOW cap exists because salary, RSUs and group insurance are all the same employer.

nodes.label: Core-Satellite 75/25 Equity Structure
nodes.rationale: ≥75% of equity flows go to index instruments; the ≤25% satellite sleeve is where agent stock-picking skill is bounded and measurable, so a bad sleeve cannot sink the plan.

nodes.label: Satellite Demotion Rule
nodes.rationale: Satellite sleeve underperforming its benchmark by >3% annualized over any rolling 12 months freezes the sleeve to index-only pending an owner-reviewed post-mortem.

nodes.label: Investment Policy Statement (IPS)
nodes.rationale: Binding, versioned document so every recommendation must cite a clause; changes require owner action outside a drawdown plus 48h cooling-off, which prevents the policy being rewritten under emotional stress.

nodes.label: Kolkata Flat Exclusion
nodes.rationale: Non-negotiable family asset housing the owner's parents at ₹0 yield; never an optimization target, never a sale or rent candidate.

nodes.label: Milestone M1: Term Life Cover
nodes.rationale: ₹2 Cr personal term cover before the child arrives; employer group cover evaporates on exit and the maximum-dependency point is now, so the agent nags until it is done.

nodes.label: ServiceNow RSU Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Modelled from a seeded grant table because no Fidelity retail API exists; base case includes $20k/yr refreshers with a no-refresher downside scenario maintained alongside.

nodes.label: Shutdown Criterion
nodes.rationale: An advisory agent that cannot beat 'index the core, prepay debt, do nothing else' after 24 months of scored operation should be simplified back to that baseline — the product is allowed to conclude it is unnecessary.

nodes.label: Daily schedule workflow
nodes.rationale: Cron 04:30 UTC = 10:00 IST, chosen to run after overnight batch processing but before market hours; expires orders, resurfaces deferred ones, records T+2/T+7 reminders.

nodes.label: DATABASE_URL (Supabase service-role pooler string)
nodes.rationale: Must be the owner/service-role pooler string on port 6543: migration 0004 enables RLS on every table with no policies, so anon and authenticated keys are denied outright and only the owner role bypasses.

nodes.label: keepalive workflow (Supabase free-tier ping)
nodes.rationale: Sundays 04:00 UTC. It is an audit_log write, not an HTTP ping, because the free tier pauses on database inactivity. Largely subsumed by the daily sync, kept belt-and-braces.

nodes.label: pnpm schedule (order expiry and reminders)
nodes.rationale: Requires the order_intents table from migration 0016_approval_orders.sql; all tasks are idempotent via idempotency keys.

nodes.label: Supabase hosted Postgres project
nodes.rationale: Free tier, Mumbai region (ref uqzbocoujennfhdqppdl), migrated and seeded 2026-08-24 with RLS verified on all 18 tables.

nodes.label: RLS-everywhere with owner-role bypass
nodes.rationale: Row level security is on for every table with zero policies, so anon/authenticated keys are denied outright while the owner role bypasses and jobs keep working. Verified with `select tablename, rowsecurity from pg_tables where schemaname='public'` — every row must read `t`. tests/db/immutability.test.ts asserts this but only against PGlite, so the real project must be checked by hand.

nodes.label: Subagent-Driven Execution Model
nodes.rationale: implementer to task reviewer to fix loop (<=5 rounds) to scoped re-review to ledger entry; briefs are stale on the Db interface so every dispatch must restate it verbatim.

nodes.label: Db Interface Contract (query/exec/withTransaction/close)
nodes.rationale: The shipped interface has four methods, not the two the plan's briefs describe; exec exists because multi-statement SQL needs the simple protocol, and withTransaction goes through sql.begin() because postgres-js is a pool where raw begin/commit can land on different connections.

nodes.label: Deferred Minors Ledger
nodes.rationale: Tracked but not blocking, with an expected home rather than a hard schedule; genuinely cross-cutting items (unwrapped batch writes, the untested postgres-js path) stay for the fix wave while anything in a file you touch is fixed on the spot.

nodes.label: src/config/ips-v1.ts as a Template Literal
nodes.rationale: Converting the IPS from a .md read at module scope to a TS template literal deleted the domain-ips-shim and its NormalModuleReplacementPlugin — and exposed a bug the shim had masked: postgres-js returns a Date for timestamptz while PGlite returns a string, so any Promise<{...: string}> over a timestamp column is a lie the PGlite suite cannot catch.

nodes.label: Never Feed JSON.stringify to a ::jsonb Placeholder
nodes.norm_label: never feed json.stringify to a ::jsonb placeholder
nodes.rationale: postgres-js stores a stringified object as a jsonb SCALAR STRING, so payload->>'...' reads NULL and the whole production audit trail was SQL-opaque; PGlite parses either form, which is why 417 green tests missed it. Fixed at all 8 write sites by passing the object.

nodes.label: PGlite vs postgres-js Driver Divergences
nodes.rationale: PGlite returns bigint columns as JS numbers and date columns as Date objects, and is a single connection so a query on the outer Db still lands inside an open transaction — which means transaction wrapping must be mutation-checked by removing withTransaction outright, not by moving a statement out of it.

nodes.label: GitHub Actions secrets as the only secret store
nodes.norm_label: github actions secrets as the only secret store
nodes.rationale: PRD hard constraint: secrets live in GitHub Actions secrets / Vercel env vars, never in the repo, the DB, or a fixture.

nodes.label: Headless four-piece deployment topology
nodes.rationale: Phase 0 is not a hosted website: it is Supabase (DB) + a private Telegram bot (messenger) + GitHub Actions cron jobs (compute) + Vercel (read-only UI), all on free tiers, with secrets in Actions.

nodes.label: Vercel-hosted read-only web app
nodes.rationale: Next.js 15 with root directory `web`, single-owner and unlisted rather than authenticated. Every portfolio view is read-only; /import is the sole write path (upload, LLM extraction, owner confirm, DB write). No Kite credentials or order placement reach the web tier.

nodes.label: No trading paths / no autonomous execution
nodes.norm_label: no trading paths / no autonomous execution
nodes.rationale: No F&O, intraday, leverage or loan-against-securities. These are absent code paths, not disabled features — there is no override flag, and every order needs fresh human approval.

nodes.label: Plus-or-minus 1% reconciliation DoD
nodes.rationale: Per-account digest figures must agree with Kite, INDmoney and Fidelity NetBenefits within 1% before the system is trusted — an external ground truth rather than internal self-consistency.

nodes.label: Phase 0 — data layer and daily digest
nodes.norm_label: phase 0 — data layer and daily digest
nodes.rationale: Delivers net worth, liabilities, allocation drift, concentration, buckets, milestones, RSU projection and a freshness verdict. DoD: digest figures agree with Kite / INDmoney / Fidelity within plus-or-minus 1%.

nodes.label: Phase 1 ("Think") — recommendation engine
nodes.rationale: FR-10 through FR-15 built on the existing schema. The agent scores, sizes, gates and scores-after-the-fact entirely on paper; nothing executes and there is no code path that could.

nodes.label: Sentinel (personal investment intelligence agent)
nodes.rationale: Single-user, approval-gated, built from a frozen PRD. Advisory only — no trading paths, no autonomous execution, no multi-tenancy.

nodes.label: Approval Expiry Policy (EOD / 7 days)
nodes.rationale: Market approvals expire at end of trading day via the NSE session calendar; SIP/MF changes after 7 days. There is no universal 72-hour expiry, and limit-order lifetime is an explicit open owner decision rather than an invented default.

nodes.label: Task 4: Web Approval/Cleanup/Rail Surfaces
nodes.rationale: Extends the existing standalone Next.js app rather than relocating to web/src/app; no OHLC charts when only close data exists, and single-owner auth is required before remote deployment.

nodes.label: Task 10: Web /advisor Surface
nodes.rationale: Shows system no-action separately and offers no approval button for a HOLD/WAIT order that does not exist; rating review and G-sec reminders stay flagged as unresolved manual coverage.

nodes.label: Telegram Approval Workflow
nodes.rationale: Approve / Modify / Defer / Reject / Show alternates on inline buttons; the human gate is the primary containment for LLM error, so there are no standing auto-execute rules.

nodes.label: Kite Deep-Link Bridge
nodes.rationale: NSE's retail algo framework requires a registered static IP for API placement; opening a pre-filled order in the Kite app for one-tap placement is zero-infra, compliant and adequate at ≤4 actions/month, keeping static-IP friction off the critical path.

nodes.label: Human-in-Loop Session Unlock
nodes.rationale: Kite access tokens expire daily; the owner completes OAuth+TOTP on phone per session. Storing no broker password or TOTP secret is the security model, not a limitation.

nodes.label: Telegram Bot Channel
nodes.rationale: Free Bot API is the primary interaction surface; the bot is locked to the owner's chat ID and ignores every other ID.

nodes.label: Zerodha Kite Connect Integration
nodes.rationale: Personal tier chosen because it is free and gives orders, GTT and Coin MF orders; it provides no market data, so prices come from NSE bhavcopy instead.

nodes.label: Sole-User / SEBI RIA Boundary
nodes.rationale: SEBI Registered Investment Adviser regulation and the whole liability posture change the moment a second person receives the output as advice, so the builder must not add features easing recommendation sharing; a second user requires RIA analysis before a single line of code.

nodes.label: Task 6: LLM ADVISE + Gated Paper Handoff
nodes.norm_label: task 6: llm advise + gated paper handoff
nodes.rationale: Sign-off creates a fresh Phase 2 request through an external authorized adapter and cannot itself approve an order; monthly caps, paper mode and freeze/breaker apply across all recommendation sources, with no separate advisor quota.

nodes.label: Task 8: Bounded Commentary
nodes.rationale: ≤300 words/section with numeric claims bound to a specific input field, unit, subject and period, because a regex checking that a numeral occurs somewhere in JSON is a lint, not semantic validation — the right number can name the wrong company, sign or period.

nodes.label: News Ingestion (news_events / news_fetch_runs)
nodes.rationale: NSE announcements and business-news RSS are candidate sources needing real format fixtures and symbol resolution before being called supported; corrections append a superseding event and weekend news is still fetched because news does not follow the NSE calendar.

nodes.label: Versioned Sentiment Classification
nodes.rationale: Reclassification appends and readers select the latest available by their own cutoff, not latest now. Unresolvable identity is flagged unresolved, never coerced to NEUTRAL/LOW, and no sentiment numeric output feeds engine scores. A buyback is not necessarily positive.

nodes.label: Alternate Generation (primary + 2)
nodes.rationale: Alternate 1 = same intent different instrument, Alternate 2 = different intent (including do-nothing or debt prepayment), so the owner always sees a real choice set rather than a single take-it-or-leave-it action.

nodes.label: Fetch Coverage Semantics
nodes.rationale: A successful empty fetch means 'no matching news in that scope', not feed failure and not proof no adverse event exists. Freshness is measured from successful coverage checks, never the latest article timestamp, so a dead feed cannot masquerade as a quiet market.
nodes.source_location: Honest data coverage and failure semantics

nodes.label: LLM Selects, Code Sizes and Gates
nodes.norm_label: llm selects, code sizes and gates
nodes.rationale: The LLM chooses an eligible (candidateId, action, timing); deterministic code attaches the exact supported size and rechecks hard gates. Selection is not a numeric score or size input, HOLD/WAIT creates no order, and negative news alone cannot manufacture an eligible SELL or override a minimum hold.

nodes.label: System No-Action vs LLM HOLD/WAIT
nodes.rationale: A missing key, timeout or malformed LLM result is recorded as unavailable — never neutral sentiment or a confident HOLD — so an outage can never be read as a considered decision to do nothing.

nodes.label: LLM Narrates, Code Decides
nodes.rationale: Deterministic code computes all scores, caps, taxes and screens; the LLM may never originate a number that feeds a rail or a score. LLM error is contained by construction plus the human approval gate.

nodes.label: screener-reminder workflow
nodes.rationale: Weekly Monday 07:00 UTC rather than a quarterly cron: the job itself checks staleness, so a weekly data-driven poll is robust where a fragile quarterly schedule would silently drift.

nodes.label: Owner-locked Telegram bot
nodes.rationale: Created via @BotFather; the owner must message the bot first because bots cannot initiate. Delivery verified end-to-end 2026-08-24.

nodes.label: TELEGRAM_OWNER_CHAT_ID
nodes.rationale: The bot is locked to this single chat id; every other id is ignored (PRD 4.1, 12.3). It is read once out of the getUpdates reply and never committed.

nodes.label: .env is not auto-loaded (no dotenv dependency)
nodes.rationale: Only `pnpm indmoney:login` uses `tsx --env-file=.env`, and web/next.config.ts parses the root .env itself. Every other script sees only shell-exported variables — the cause of the recurring 'Missing required environment variable: TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN'.

nodes.label: deploy-dashboard job (GitHub Pages)
nodes.rationale: Second job gated on `needs: weekly`; the report job writes docs/dashboard.html, which is uploaded as a Pages artifact and then deployed. Splitting deploy from generation keeps id-token/pages permissions off the job that holds the DB and Telegram secrets.

nodes.label: weekly-report workflow
nodes.rationale: Sunday 04:30 UTC = 10:00 IST per PRD 12.2; owner signed off the Saturday 08:00 to Sunday 10:00 move on 2026-09-13. GitHub cron is best-effort, so a few minutes of slip is expected and tolerated.

nodes.label: Branded bigint paise/cents (no floats)
nodes.rationale: Every money path uses branded bigint minor units; a float anywhere in a money path is a correctness bug, and the brand makes it a type error instead.

nodes.label: GSEC_YIELD_PCT (owner-supplied, never invented)
nodes.rationale: There is no ingestion source for the 10Y G-sec yield, so it is a required caller input. Blank means 'not configured' and the signal review states it did not run — never 0%.

nodes.label: pnpm report (weekly deep report FR-51)
nodes.rationale: Five sections: signal review, watchlist changes, recommendation pipeline, staleness plus blocked names, scoring and narrative. `--as-of YYYY-MM-DD` reproduces a past week.

nodes.label: Optional LLM_API_KEY degrades loudly
nodes.rationale: An unset GitHub secret interpolates to ''. Absent or blank LLM_API_KEY means no narration and no satellite scoring, and the report states that rather than guessing a value.

nodes.label: Blank-but-present DATABASE_URL throws
nodes.rationale: An unset GitHub secret interpolates to ''. Falling back to embedded PGlite would show a plausible-looking Rs 0 net worth, so the code refuses instead: unset the variable entirely or give it a real URL.

nodes.label: What the engine will not invent
nodes.norm_label: what the engine will not invent
nodes.rationale: The G-sec yield, a cost basis it cannot read, a tax figure, a rating action, and a hit-rate from fewer than 20 evaluations in a bucket. Unknown cost basis is NULL, never 0; an unknown is never rendered as Rs 0.

nodes.label: Encrypted pg_dump Backup + Tested Restore
nodes.rationale: Restore must be verified in an isolated database covering rows, constraints and immutable history; no production overwrite.

nodes.label: Task 5: Paper Scheduling, Scoring, Backup/Restore
nodes.rationale: Expiry is enforced at every action/read boundary rather than trusting cron delivery; a runbook without a tested restore into an isolated database does not satisfy Phase 2.

nodes.label: Task 7: Calibration by Conviction and Horizon
nodes.norm_label: task 7: calibration by conviction and horizon
nodes.rationale: Counts distinct eligible recommendations, not 3/6/12m observations as three independent calls; provisional minimum N=20 per bucket, unelapsed outcomes excluded with reasons rather than counted as misses, and retrospective replay is never mixed into the forward scorecard.

nodes.label: Point-in-Time Deterministic Replay
nodes.rationale: Cuts off both economic and availability/ingestion timestamps so a late import carrying an old as_of cannot leak backward; never replays today's watchlist or portfolio across old dates as point-in-time.

nodes.label: Conviction Calibration
nodes.rationale: HIGH conviction must outperform MEDIUM over trailing 12 months or the conviction model is flagged; systematic overconfidence is itself a breaker-review trigger.

nodes.label: Falsification Circuit Breaker
nodes.rationale: Three consecutive approved recommendations hitting their falsification conditions self-demote the agent to report-only; reset requires an explicit owner command plus an agent-generated post-mortem.

nodes.label: Recommendation Scorecard
nodes.rationale: Benchmark is stored at creation time so scoring cannot be retrofitted; scoring at 3/6/12 months also measures whether owner modifications and rejections added or subtracted value.

nodes.label: Retrospective Experiment Caveat
nodes.rationale: Running a new model over old news is a retrospective experiment with training-data leakage, model drift and nondeterminism — not a point-in-time backtest, not an exact reproduction, and not free.

nodes.label: Task 3: Paper Cleanup + Multi-Year LTCG Calendar
nodes.norm_label: task 3: paper cleanup + multi-year ltcg calendar
nodes.rationale: Shipped as src/domain/cleanup.ts + src/jobs/cleanup.ts with 14 tests. Existing aggregate owner-cost lots are not reliable acquisition lots; missing history yields unknown estimates and named owner-data prerequisites, never ₹0 tax or a fabricated exemption.

nodes.label: Fidelity RSU Modelled Integration
nodes.rationale: No retail API, so vests stay PROJECTED until a quarterly owner reconciliation turns them ACTUAL; vested NOW is the largest single-stock position and is invisible to every other tool the owner has.

nodes.label: FIFO Lot Tracking
nodes.rationale: FIFO lots everywhere including seeded history; corporate actions adjust lots and every sell shows per-lot gains.

nodes.label: Legacy Cleanup Mandate
nodes.rationale: All four smallcase subscriptions terminated at v1 while their constituent ETFs are retained; consolidation is spread over 1–2 fiscal years to fit inside the ₹1.25L LTCG exemption instead of triggering a single large tax event.

nodes.label: LTCG Harvest Planner
nodes.rationale: Proposes harvest transactions each fiscal year to consume the ₹1.25L equity LTCG exemption against the cleanup program.

nodes.label: Schedule FA / ClearTax Exports
nodes.rationale: Holding US-listed shares at Fidelity makes Schedule FA reporting applicable today, so foreign holdings need acquisition/peak/closing INR values exported annually.

nodes.label: Sell / Exit Triggers
nodes.rationale: Seven monthly-evaluated triggers; sell logic is first-class because the system must be demonstrably capable of recommending exits, not only entries.

nodes.label: Tax Engine
nodes.rationale: All rates parameterized in config and verified at build time, never hardcoded in logic; the engine states it computes estimates, not filings, since the audience is ClearTax self-filing.

nodes.label: Bucket B1: FI Corpus
nodes.rationale: ₹10.3–17.1 Cr real at age 55, derived from ₹3–5L/month FI income at a 3.5% SWR; the owner's original ₹40 Cr anchor was discarded as unexamined arithmetic.

nodes.label: Credit Rule (beat 7.95% loan rate)
nodes.rationale: Slab-taxed credit paper must beat the highest loan rate after tax and a credit-risk haircut; the new tax regime gives no home-loan interest deduction, which strengthens prepay-vs-invest math.

nodes.label: Loan Prepayment Cascade
nodes.rationale: Owner-locked strategy: car loan 1 EMI redirects to car loan 2 then to the home loan, closing it Dec 2033 and saving ~₹19.3L interest. Loan outflow is constant ₹55,526/mo until Dec 2033, a step function the contribution model must encode.

nodes.label: The Plan's Reference Code Is a Sketch, Not Truth
nodes.norm_label: the plan's reference code is a sketch, not truth
nodes.rationale: Tasks 2, 3, 5 and 6 each shipped a real defect in the plan's own snippet — one failing its own acceptance criterion by construction — so briefs give acceptance criteria and interfaces, and an implementer that contradicts the brief with working arithmetic is doing its job.

nodes.label: Loan Cascade — Owner-Verified Figures and Closures
nodes.norm_label: loan cascade — owner-verified figures and closures
nodes.rationale: Every loan comes from a real lender statement and reconciles arithmetically, so the PRD's stale 36.7L total loses. The plan's reference runCascade amortized sequentially and failed its own flat-outflow criterion by construction; the concurrent rewrite is correct. Closure dates are derived from closures, never written as literals — two earlier literal sets in this file were wrong.

nodes.label: Planning Assumptions (PRD 15.2)
nodes.rationale: salaryStepUp is a separate key from sipStepUp on purpose (equal today, must not be re-merged) because take-home and SIP escalation are independent decisions.

nodes.label: Investable Surplus Curve
nodes.rationale: 82,124/month is derived, never hardcoded, and the ~6,124 gap against the PRD's 76,000 is an open owner true-up — not electricity, which the misc bucket already includes. The coverage guard keys off the outflow map's own range because closures is persisted nowhere and would silently no-op for a consumer reading a schedule back from Postgres.

nodes.label: Weekly backup workflow
nodes.rationale: Runs Sunday 05:30 UTC (11:00 IST) with a 30-minute timeout; encrypted pg_dump pushed to a private backup repo so the only copy of owner financial state is not the free-tier Supabase project.

nodes.label: BACKUP_REPO / BACKUP_BRANCH / GH_TOKEN
nodes.rationale: A separate private GitHub repo holds the encrypted dumps, pushed with a PAT carrying `repo` scope — keeping backups out of the application repo.

nodes.label: One-time interactive INDmoney OAuth login
nodes.rationale: Human-in-loop unlock is the security model: no broker password or TOTP secret is stored, only an encrypted portfolio:read refresh token. The token must be created against the Supabase DB, not the local .pglite, or CI cannot see it.

nodes.label: pnpm backup (encrypted pg_dump)
nodes.rationale: AES-256-GCM encrypted dump pushed to the private backup repo; `backup:restore` needs the same key and an empty target DB.

nodes.label: TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY
nodes.rationale: One 32-byte base64 key used everywhere — the INDmoney login encrypts the refresh token with it and CI sync decrypts with it. If the local and CI values diverge, sync silently falls back to the file snapshot and the login must be re-run.

nodes.label: Task 6: Provisioning, Handoff, Phase 2 Acceptance
nodes.rationale: Tests cannot replace four elapsed weeks or five owner interactions; evidence must be dated, and an inherited test count is not proof.

nodes.label: INDmoney Advisory-Only Path
nodes.rationale: No public order-placement API exists, so actions are instruct → owner executes in-app → verify on next sync → nag at T+2/T+7. The asymmetry is designed for explicitly; INDmoney actions are never presented as executable.

nodes.label: PRD Phase 2 — Prove
nodes.rationale: DoD: 4 clean weeks of paper operation, ≥5 end-to-end owner approval interactions, a rendering scorecard, and a simulated rail violation plus breaker trip both behaving to spec.

nodes.label: PRD Phase 3 — Act
nodes.rationale: Gated on owner review of the paper scorecard; introduces real Kite execution, tax engine v1 and armed caps/breakers.

nodes.label: Known Data Coverage Gaps
nodes.rationale: Unavailable 2026 index-series feed, no EV/EBITDA or own 5y P/E history, partial fundamental/identity coverage, aggregate rather than complete FIFO lots, and a static owner-provided G-sec value. No source or model fills these from recall to make a recommendation pass.

nodes.label: Task 9: Owner-Signed Quarterly Watchlist Revision
nodes.rationale: Removals evaluate watchlist evidence, not only sell triggers on owned positions, and insufficient history is not a failure signal. Append-only watchlist history must not be UPDATE-d to set removed_on — add a version/event representation rather than disabling audit protection.

nodes.label: Binary Quality Gate
nodes.rationale: ROCE >15%, positive FCF in 4 of 5 years, sane D/E, zero red flags (pledging >5%, auditor resignation, SEBI action) — must-pass before any score matters.

nodes.label: Quarterly screener.in CSV Upload
nodes.rationale: A 10-minute owner task replaces a paid fundamentals feed; it is the only source for the quality gate inputs.

nodes.label: Satellite Stock Signal Stack
nodes.rationale: Composite 0–100 with valuation 30%, trend 30%, earnings direction 20%, fit 20%; score ≥70 required. Trend is weighted heavily specifically so the system never buys quality in freefall.

nodes.label: Zero-Cost Data Budget
nodes.rationale: Total data cost is ₹0 in v1; the accepted consequence is fundamental coverage limited to the ~40-name watchlist, with full-market screening deferred 2–3 years until a paid feed is justified.

nodes.label: funded_status Architecture Test
nodes.rationale: funded_status must not reach drafting, sizing, rails, risk or recommendation logic, including through reporting helpers or payload injection.

nodes.label: src/advisor/ Layer
nodes.rationale: Consumes explicitly projected read-only engine/context DTOs; pure engine and sizing computations are allowed for offline replay but persistence helpers, broker adapters and arbitrary SQL writes are not.

nodes.label: Funded Status vs FI Band
nodes.rationale: Reporting-only metric computed monthly against the ₹10.3–17.1 Cr real FI band.

nodes.label: Advisor Capability Firewall
nodes.rationale: Capabilities are split rather than imports prohibited: separate proposal, replay and news writers, with an owner-action service outside src/advisor/ as the only path that converts a proposal into a paper request. Architecture tests must cover transitive paths and injected capabilities, not just direct import strings.

nodes.label: No-Catch-Up Rule
nodes.rationale: Funded-status is unreadable by any sizing or risk function, enforced as a code-level property, because a shortfall must never justify taking more risk to catch up.
